subsystems.name: Atomic vapour cell
subsystems.role: holds the alkali metal vapour in which Rydberg atoms are created and probed.
parts: alkali metal reservoir (e.g. rubidium or caesium)

subsystems.name: Laser system
subsystems.role: excites atoms to high-lying Rydberg states via a two-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) scheme.

subsystems.name: Optical detection
subsystems.role: measures the transmitted probe beam to record the EIT spectrum.

subsystems.name: RF coupling
subsystems.role: delivers the radio-frequency field under test to the atoms.
parts: optional reference field for phase measurement

subsystems.name: Magnetic field control
subsystems.role: cancels stray magnetic fields that would shift Rydberg energy levels and broaden the EIT line.

subsystems.name: Signal processing and calibration
subsystems.role: extracts amplitude and phase from the EIT spectrum and converts them to field units using atomic constants.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the vapour cell
buildSteps.detail: A glass cell is blown and loaded with a small amount of alkali metal, then sealed under vacuum; a heater and temperature sensor are attached to control vapour density.

buildSteps.title: Set up the laser system
buildSteps.detail: Probe and coupling diode lasers are mounted, their frequencies locked to atomic transitions using saturation spectroscopy or similar techniques.

buildSteps.title: Align the optical path
buildSteps.detail: The two laser beams are combined, directed through the vapour cell, and aligned to maximise the EIT transmission peak.

buildSteps.title: Integrate RF coupling
buildSteps.detail: The cell is placed in a known RF environment — a waveguide, a horn, or free space — so the field to be measured interacts with the atoms.

buildSteps.title: Shield magnetic fields
buildSteps.detail: A mu-metal enclosure and compensation coils reduce the ambient magnetic field to below the level that would disturb the Rydberg states.

buildSteps.title: Characterise EIT without RF
buildSteps.detail: The transmitted probe power is recorded as the coupling laser frequency is scanned, establishing the baseline EIT line shape.

buildSteps.title: Apply RF and measure the spectrum
buildSteps.detail: The RF field is switched on; it splits or shifts the EIT peak by an amount proportional to the field strength, and the new spectrum is recorded.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and validate
buildSteps.detail: The measured splitting is converted to electric field units using atomic dipole moments and fundamental constants, then compared with a conventional calibrated antenna in a known field.

prerequisites.tech: Rydberg atoms and electromagnetically induced transparency
prerequisites.why: the sensing mechanism relies on well-understood atomic physics and laser spectroscopy.
stable, narrow-line lasers are needed to resolve the EIT feature and lock to atomic transitions.
commercial cells provide a convenient, room-temperature medium for Rydberg excitation.
Rydberg levels are highly sensitive to magnetic fields, so shielding is required for accurate measurements.
theory is well developed, but extending it to arbitrary field configurations and high accuracy is still an active area.
today's demonstrations are laboratory setups; shrinking them into portable, robust instruments remains to be done.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of self-calibrated RF field measurement using Rydberg EIT
pathway.unlocks: a calibration-free alternative to conventional antennas for metrology.

pathway.milestone: improved sensitivity, bandwidth and dynamic range through better lasers, cells and detection
pathway.unlocks: measurement of weaker fields and broader frequency coverage.

pathway.milestone: field trials for antenna calibration, RF metrology and communications
pathway.unlocks: practical validation against established standards in real environments.

pathway.milestone: commercial traceable RF field probes, possibly chip-scale
